items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: I joined Hardy's band -- I think I went to Chicago to join that band.

ctx.x: And so I joined Hardy, it must've been oh, let me see now. I joined Hardy's band -- I think I went to Chicago to join that band. Cause that was their headquarters. And they worked out of Chicago. Eddie Mallory was a trumpet player in the band. And Charlie Turner, bass player. That's right, I went to Chicago and joined that band. And their headquarters out of Chicago. We did one-night stands all over everywhere, Iowa and Chicago, jumping out of cars and I stayed with that band until I got an offer to go to the…
Now that must've been very exciting.

items.title: Doc Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 28, 1995
items.q: I came back and I recorded with Marion Harding — Alabamians, a band out of Chicago. That’s the band that Cab Calloway took over. And I played with Harding

ctx.x: No kidding, that’s good, it got recorded.

Yes it did. And I came back in 1930. I left Sam over there because I got tired of being over there. I came back and I recorded with Marion Harding — Alabamians, a band out of Chicago. That’s the band that Cab Calloway took over. And I played with Harding, and then I went to McKinney’s Cotton Pickers in Detroit. And I recorded oh a lot of things with that band. Then from there I went to the Cotton Club with Cab Calloway and I stayed there nine years. And we made so many recordings, 78s with Cab, we made so many I…
Well we want you to stay too.
